transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Mark DeLuca (LatencyWorks CTO), Jenna Park (Platform PM), Omar Khan (Head of Security), Liu Wei (SRE)
---
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros, and then Priya will walk through the hybrid refarch we sketched.
[00:28] Mark (LatencyWorks): Hi all, Mark here, quick note we're looking to list on Redwood marketplace once we validate the hybrid flow and security guards. Jenna and Omar will co-own the integration.
[01:02] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, I sent the initial refarch earlier — it's basically Hosted API for burst + Private (VPC) for sensitive traffic, with an on-prem connector for air-gapped customers. We'll show how the KV cache and prefix caching slots map into the edge nodes.
[01:45] Jenna (LatencyWorks): When you say edge nodes, are those Redwood-managed in region or do we need to provision compute in our VPC? We want to avoid too many egress charges and also keep PII on-prem.
[02:10] Priya: Good question. The pattern we recommend is regional Redwood edge (hosted) for low-latency public requests; for PII or regulated requests you route to Private nodes in your VPC via VPC peering or PrivateLink. The on-prem connector can host a small inference pool inside your subnet for fully air-gapped flows.
[02:47] Liu (LatencyWorks SRE): Peering is fine but we need specifics: ports, NAT, DNS, and the expected egress / burst rate. Jenna, we have a strict egress rule out of corp network.
[03:15] Alex: We'll add a network checklist. Priya, is there a known firewall footprint we usually ask partners to open?
[03:30] Priya: Typically we need outbound TLS to our control plane (443) plus dedicated ports for the inference tunnel if using on-prem connector; I'll put exact IP ranges in the checklist. Also note our KV cache synchronization is over mTLS and can be routed over the peered link.
[04:00] Omar (Head of Security): On KMS — we use an HSM via internal KMS provider. How do we manage key wrapping for model artifacts and logs?
[04:20] Priya: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and HSM. For marketplace listing, we document the support matrix. For audit logs we can stream to your SIEM, or you can pull via API. We need to confirm retention and whether logs contain any sensitive token data (we can redact).
[05:05] Mark: SOC2 is a must for our procurement. Do you have a short pack?
[05:15] Alex: Yes, we'll share a security pack — SOC2 summary, pen test attestations, SSO and RBAC docs. Expect that in the shared folder today.
[05:45] Jenna: Packaging — we lean Helm for internal ops. For marketplace listing, do you require a specific operator or is a packaged Helm chart enough?
[06:03] Priya: Helm chart is fine. For Private marketplace listing we add a connector repo and a small operator to ease upgrades. For the on-prem path we recommend a lightweight Helm chart plus a service account and CRD for version pinning.
[06:45] Liu: How do upgrades work? We have to validate upgrades in our UAT before pushing prod.
[07:00] Priya: Our operator supports canary upgrades and rollback. For Private/on-prem we provide a manifest to run in UAT; our rollout tool can be configured to pause for your manual approval step.
[07:30] Alex: Let's talk performance. Jenna, can you share expected RPS and 95th latency targets?
[07:45] Jenna: For baseline: 200 RPS with 95th < 250ms for non-PII requests, and spike to 800 RPS during peak. For PII flows we need 95th < 350ms but must stay inside Private nodes.
[08:10] Priya: That profile helps. For the dedicated SKU we usually recommend 2x the baseline to allow batching and headroom. We'll run a smoke benchmark with a representative prompt set.
[08:35] Mark: Cost is a factor — we compare Redwood Dedicated vs hosting ourselves on cloud GPUs. Do you have ballpark unit economics?
[08:50] Alex: We'll include a pricing sheet. The Dedicated model gives you predictable throughput and lower unit cost at commit, plus the operational burden offloaded. We discussed earlier that ModelServeCo was cheaper for pure throughput but lacked the hybrid VPC tooling.
[09:20] Omar: Regarding logs and retention, any PII in logs is a dealbreaker. We need clear guarantees.
[09:35] Priya: We can redact PII at the edge via prefix filters, and we offer configurable retention. We'll add a note in the security pack about redaction knobs and audit streams.
[10:10] Mark: For the marketplace listing itself, what's the checklist? Who signs off?
[10:25] Alex: The listing checklist includes: product description + assets, pricing proposal, deployment docs (Helm chart), security pack (SOC2, KMS, SSO), network checklist, and a short reference architecture diagram. Sign-off is typically by Redwood listings PM after SE review and legal review on both sides.
[11:00] Jenna: Timeline: we want listing live before our next sales push in mid-April. Is that feasible?
[11:15] Alex: If we run the pilot ASAP and get security docs in the next two weeks, mid-April is tight but doable.
[11:35] Priya: Operational detail — KV cache warm-up: we recommend preloading common prefixes during deployment to hit cold-start objectives. Also quantization profile — if you want smaller memory footprint on on-prem pool, we can recommend 4-bit quantization profiles and point to the model variants that have been validated.
[12:05] Liu: Any compatibility matrix for GPUs vs CPU? Some of our on-prem racks are older.
[12:20] Priya: We'll include a compatibility table in the refarch doc; older GPUs may need different kernel selection or be CPU-only fallbacks. We support fallback routing so requests can go to hosted nodes if the on-prem pool can't meet latency.
[12:55] Mark: Let's nail the pilot scope. We want a short pilot: run 48-hour smoke at expected baseline RPS, verify privacy flows in Private nodes, and confirm SLOs and logging.
[13:20] Priya: Agreed. Pilot steps: 1) share traffic profile and sample prompts; 2) Redwood provisions a dedicated pilot pool or uses a compatible hosted variant; 3) run smoke with our tooling and share tokenized logs + metrics; 4) iterate on config (batching, cache TTLs, quantization).
[14:00] Jenna: On contracts — procurement will want clear liability and data handling terms. We'll loop in legal if pilot looks good.
[14:15] Alex: Noted. We'll send a draft pilot terms of engagement for review.
[14:40] Omar: One more on identity — SSO and RBAC: we need SAML and SCIM support for provisioning service accounts.
[15:00] Priya: We support SAML SSO for the console and SCIM for user provisioning. For machine-to-machine we use signed JWTs and mTLS for connector tunnels.
[15:30] Mark: Any blockers you see from Redwood side?
[15:40] Alex: Main things we need: your traffic profile, network diagram, and confirmation of KMS provider. We'll send the listing checklist and security pack.
[16:05] Jenna: OK we'll aim to get that by Friday.
[16:20] Liu: We'll also attach our UAT networking rules.
[16:35] Alex: Great. Last bit — who owns the marketplace marketing blurb and screenshots?
[16:45] Jenna: Marketing will own assets, but we may need some example prompts and output snippets from Redwood for the listing.
[17:00] Alex: We'll coordinate with your marketer.
[17:20] Priya: I'll draft the refarch diagram and include notes about KV cache sync and preloading.
[17:40] Mark: Perfect. Anything else?
[17:50] Alex: No, just to recap action items: Redwood will share security pack + checklist; Priya will share diagram; LatencyWorks will share traffic profile and KMS details. We'll schedule the pilot planning meeting next week.
[18:15] Jenna: Thanks everyone.
[18:25] Omar: Thanks.
[18:30] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears (e.g., connector tunnel sometimes transcribed as "connector tunnel" vs "connect or tunnel"), product names abbreviated in places.
